data.title: Fix the energy and time of the particles in EDMToHepMCConverter
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
- `EDMToHepMCConverter`: fix the particle energy (was set to the mass) and the vertex time (was divided by c instead of multiplied)
- `FlatSmearVertex`: fix the time offset for events shifted along the beam (was dz/c instead of dz)

ENDRELEASENOTES

Two small bugs I found while looking at #61. HepMC3 stores the vertex time as c*t in length units (its unit conversion [scales t like x, y, z](https://gitlab.cern.ch/hepmc/HepMC3/-/blob/3.3.1/include/HepMC3/Units.h#L94-107), and DD4hep's reader [divides by c](https://github.com/AIDASoft/DD4hep/blob/ba3ad338feb2c61e318b1f71c71126a34b7982c5/DDG4/hepmc/HepMC3EventReader.cpp#L103)), while EDM4hep's `MCParticle::time` [is in ns](https://github.com/key4hep/EDM4hep/blob/682d691167e2b31f8489a9b1f58fa24a2698c517/edm4hep.yaml#L249…

data.title: [TrackFitter] Add reset of the global TGeoManager navigator before fitting each track
data.author: andread3vita
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
- Reset the global TGeoManager navigator to a canonical state before each fit. The navigator state is process-global and is modified by material lookups during track extrapolation. Without this reset, the material assigned to points located on geometry boundaries may depend on the previously fitted track, potentially from an earlier event, making the fit results dependent on processing order.
- Remove isPositiveSemiDefinite from utils.

ENDRELEASENOTES

Dear All,
I open this PR to introduce a reset of the TGeoManager before each fit. Thank you!

Cheers,
Andrea

data.title: Preserve state changes on hits when steps are filtered out
data.author: trholmes
data.body:
This is a proposed long-term fix for the problem described in this ticket (and several tickets):
https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/issues/538

In many scenarios where the step-size was the same order as sensor thicknesses, we'd see short steps that end with an exit of the volume but don't deposit enough energy to make it past the 1 keV (or occasionally even the 0 energy) filter. The step would then be removed by the filter and the hit wouldn't close, continuing until it reached another sensor. The resulting hit would take on the average position between the two sensors, creating hit locations outside the sensor (and sometimes appearing in a stripe at z=0 when the two sensors are in either endcap).

This PR creates a new function that retains state changes when a step is filtered out. T…

data.title: Fix O(N^2) loops in CreateTruthLinks
data.author: davidlange6
data.body:
Three inner loops each iterated over all MCParticles to find non-zero entries, giving O(N_hits × N_particles) and O(N_cluster_hits × N_links) complexity.

primary changes: 1) Iterate simHitMapEnergy map keys directly instead of scanning all MCParticles for non-zero entries. 2)Build a cellID → links index (std::unordered_map) once after the calo-hit loop, then use O(1) lookup per cluster hit instead of a full scan of the link collection. 3) Iiterate mcpEnergy map keys directly instead of scanning all MCParticles per cluster.

BEGINRELEASENOTES
- Speedup O(N2) loops in CreateTruthLinks
ENDRELEASENOTES

comments.author: scott-snyder

comments.author: davidlange6
comments.body: I did an element-by-element comparison of CaloHitMCParticleLinks and ClusterMCParticleLinks including their order. The intent is that using ordered maps should preserve results.

data.title: Use CTest fixtures for generated test data
data.author: jmcarcell
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
- CMake: Use CTest fixtures for generated test data in DDSim and the examples. Selecting a consumer automatically includes its producers, and failed setup skips consumers instead of producing secondary missing-file errors.
- CMake: Use a fixture for DDDB extraction and cleanup, and allow cleanup when the database is absent.

ENDRELEASENOTES

Fixtures are different from `DEPENDS` in that the tests won't run if their setup test wasn't successful, while `DEPENDS` only indicates that a test has to run after another one.

## Summary

Extends the `k4BenchAuditor` with additional per-component performance metrics to better understand where Gaudi jobs spend resources beyond CPU and wall-clock time.

The auditor now records:

- **Heap allocations:** Number of allocations, allocated bytes, net allocated bytes, peak heap usage, and largest allocation.
- **Hardware counters:** Instructions executed and CPU cycles, providing metrics that are less sensitive to system load than timing measurements.
- **Page faults:** Minor and major faults to help identify memory access and I/O overhead.
- **Context switches:** Voluntary and involuntary switches to identify blocking and scheduling interference.

data.title: feat(plugin): add a Gaudi auditor that records per-component costs of k4run jobs
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
## Summary

This PR adds a Gaudi auditor to measure the performance of individual algorithms and services in `k4run` jobs, laying the groundwork for extending k4Bench to reconstruction benchmarking.

The new `k4BenchAuditor` records wall time, CPU time, and peak memory increases for each component, covering both event processing and lifecycle phases (initialize, start, stop, finalize). Nested calls are accounted for without double counting, allowing performance costs to be attributed to individual algorithms and their enclosing sequencers.

The auditor produces two output files:
- `_components.json` with per-component measurements, component metadata, and execution hierarchy.

data.title: refactor: centralise the run store layout and read rank-group keys by name
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
## Summary

This PR centralises the benchmark run directory layout and replaces positional rank-group tuple access with named fields.

The run store layout (`detector/platform/stack/sample/date`) was previously constructed independently in several places, making it easy for the different readers to drift apart. The main changes are:

- Introduce `k4bench.layout` and use it across remote data access, local regression reports, dashboard views, and blame tooling.

data.title: Enable TLS for database connections when available
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body:
asyncpg never requested TLS, so DBOD instances that require an
encrypted connection (like the new fcc-dami-test database) rejected
every connection attempt, crash-looping the backend on startup.
Defaults to "prefer" so existing non-TLS databases are unaffected.

data.title: Fix frontend API URL not taking effect at runtime
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body:
METADATA_BROWSER_BACKEND_URL is only read at Docker build time, so
setting it in the runtime Secret never had any effect -- the deployed
frontend was always falling back to http://localhost:8000. Documents
and adds NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, which Nitro does apply at container
startup, to the staging env template.

data.title: Rename to DaMI and add staging environment
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body:
Renames the project to Dataset Metadata Interface (DaMI) at the code
level (display strings, docstrings, frontend branding -- repo name
and registry paths unchanged), and adds a staging deploy pipeline:
pushes to main now also deploy to a new fcc-dami-test OpenShift
project backed by its own DBOD instance, while prod continues to
redeploy only on a git tag.

data.title: Add tag-triggered prod deploy
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body:
Adds a tag-triggered deploy-prod job and lets build-backend/build-frontend
run on tags too, so pushing a release tag deploys prod without requiring
another push to master. Needed to make the v0.1.1 release tag actually
trigger a pipeline.

data.title: Support HEAD requests on health endpoints
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body: `/healthz` and `/readyz` returned 405 for HEAD requests, which uptime monitors often use. Both now accept GET and HEAD.

data.title: Add /healthz and /readyz endpoints with Kubernetes probes
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body: Adds `/healthz` (liveness, no dependencies) and `/readyz` (checks the database, returns 503 when it is unavailable). The backend deployment gets startup and liveness probes on `/healthz`. `/readyz` is meant for external monitoring and is not used as a readiness probe, so the single pod keeps serving error responses during database outages. Both paths are excluded from the request logging.

data.title: Fix backend mypy error and validate backend on GitHub
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body: mypy fails in the GitLab `validate-backend` job on `master` after #9, which skips the build and deploy stages. Fixes the error and adds a GitHub Actions workflow running the same ruff and mypy checks on PRs, so such errors show up before merging.

data.title: Add CORS headers to 500 errors and hide exception details
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body:
Unhandled 500 errors bypassed `CORSMiddleware`, so the frontend showed them as CORS failures. They now carry CORS headers and no longer return the exception message to the client, and the handler logs only a one-line summary.

Refs #8

data.title: fix(HepMC3EventReader): apply the length unit to the primary vertex position
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
-  HepMC3EventReader: apply the length unit to the primary vertex position

ENDRELEASENOTES

## Summary

Apply the HepMC3 event length unit when setting the primary vertex position in `HepMC3EventReader`.

The particle production/end positions are already converted using `len_unit`, and the vertex time is converted as well, but the `x`, `y`, and `z` coordinates of the corresponding `Geant4Vertex` were previously used without applying the HepMC3 length unit.

This is invisible for HepMC3 files using millimetres, but gives incorrect vertex positions for events using centimetres.
